finding.claim: The DELETE /projects/:id handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project, including ones they don't own.
finding.source: An authenticated non-owner, non-admin user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>.

trace.note: The project is fetched by the id in the URL with no owner scoping.
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false, and the return value is discarded. The function never throws.
authorized() only returns a boolean. The throwing variant is authorize() at line 4.

finding.guards_checked: The authorize() function throws on failure, but this route calls authorized() instead, so no exception is raised. No middleware in this file does any other ownership check. Authentication of req.user happens elsewhere and is not an ownership check. The PUT route at line 25 correctly uses authorize().

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12 returns a boolean and is never tested at api.js:18. authorize() at api.js:4 throws but is only called by the PUT route at api.js:25. No other ownership middleware appears in this file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement and discards the boolean, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user. The only ownership check in the file, authorize() at api.js:4, is used on the PUT route (api.js:25) and not on DELETE.
